A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/2a68cbeceea9173ab7a53d334d073e9779b048ad8946fd3ff81b09adb79cee98.png)

From the above, we see that:

- For graph II, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, graph II shows a one-to-one function. As a result, this function is invertible.

- For graphs I, III and IV, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. These are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.

From the above, we see that:

  • For graphs I, III and IV, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. These are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.
